title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: Maintain a deque of indices whose values are strictly decreasing. The front is always the max of the current window. O(n) total because each index is pushed and popped at most once.

notes: Deque stores INDICES, not values — you need the index to know when an item slides out of the window.
Pop from the back while the tail value is smaller than nums[i]; those tails can never be the window max once nums[i] enters.
Front of the deque is the answer for the current window — record it only once i >= k-1.
Each index enters and leaves the deque at most once → amortized O(n) despite the inner while.

options: Indices whose values are strictly decreasing

questions.q: Why pop from the back while the tail value is smaller than nums[i]?
options: Those tails can never be the window max once nums[i] is in the window
It keeps the deque sorted ascending

questions.q: When do you start writing answers to the output?
options: Once i >= k - 1 (window is fully formed)

questions.explain: Each index is pushed and popped at most once, so the inner while is amortized O(1).

exercises.prompt: Fill in the monotonic-deque sliding-window maximum.

blanks.hint: boundary: index <= i - k means it left the window
drop tails that are strictly less than the new value
the front of the deque is the current max

L3.prompt: Write `maxSlidingWindow(nums, k)` returning the maximum of each window of size k. O(n). Log `JSON.stringify(maxSlidingWindow([1, 3, -1, -3, 5, 3, 6, 7], 3))`.
hints: Store indices in the deque, not values — you need the index to expire entries.
Two cleanups per step: shift the front if it left the window, pop the back while it's smaller than nums[i].
Record the front (dq[0]) only after the window is fully formed: i >= k - 1.
